scope: Synchronous app boundary calling three real owned-memory modules via path dependencies. No GUI/model dependency, worker, filesystem, publishing, tar.gz chaining or process supervision.

api.start: Operation::start() -> Result<(Operation, Cancellation), AdapterFailure>; consumes a process-local monotonic non-reused ID. Operation is not Clone and each run method consumes self.
api.gzip: Operation::gzip<E>(gzip::Request, &mut gzip::Budget, FnMut(Event<gzip::Checkpoint>) -> Result<(), gzip::Stop<E>>) -> Terminal<gzip::Completed, gzip::Error<E>>
api.ustar: Operation::ustar<E>(ustar::Request, FnOnce(&[ustar::Entry]) -> Result<Vec<String>, E>, FnMut(Event<ustar::Checkpoint>) -> Result<(), ustar::Stop>) -> Terminal<ustar::Completed, ustar::Error<E>>
api.exports: Re-export native gzip, ustar, zip_create crates, Request/Limits/Usage/checkpoint/error types without reinterpretation.
api.receiver: Receiver::new(operation.id()); progress(&Event), terminal(&Terminal) -> Result<Delivery, DeliveryError>. Check before applying UI changes or taking payload.
api.memory: Terminal::into_result() transfers Result<MemoryValidated<T>, Failure<E>>; success has private constructor and exposes native value by borrow or ownership transfer.

identity.scope: Unique within one linked library instance/process lifetime, not persisted identity or authentication. IDs 1..u64::MAX-1, exhaustion returns OperationIdExhausted, never wraps or reuses. No worker/job ID conversion.
identity.new_work: Create a fresh Operation, Cancellation and Receiver. Old handles remain bound to old operation and cannot cancel a new one. Caller explicitly chooses the current Receiver.
identity.concurrency: Caller may move Operation to its own thread and retain Cancellation; adapter creates no thread, channel, executor or queue. Callback delivery/backpressure and integration are caller-owned.

events.stamp: Private stamp contains OperationId and sequence, starting at zero per operation. Each delivered checkpoint consumes one sequence; returned Terminal consumes the next position, including no-checkpoint native errors.
events.overflow: Reserve u64::MAX for Terminal. At exhausted sequence, do not call observer; record SequenceExhausted and return native Stop::Cancelled to stop work. Terminal retains native failure and secondary adapter cause; drop any success payload if adapter fault exists. This is an explicit transport limit, not a format Budget.
events.receiver: Ignore other operation IDs before checking sequence or closed/faulted state. Current duplicate/reversal/gap fails and latches Faulted. After terminal reject current progress/duplicate terminal. Do not silently reset on mismatch.
events.receiver_failure: Receiver error is an app delivery error, not a format error or cleanup proof. Caller should separately request cancellation and handle the actual terminal; rebuilding a receiver for the same operation to hide a gap is outside the contract.
events.stages: Event contains the exact native Checkpoint, including USTAR pass/selection, ZIP validate/write/seek/finish, GZip stage and cumulative Usage. No synthetic terminal callback before native return.
events.delivery: Observer receives events synchronously and may forward them. Receiver validates ordering only, not forged metadata or external authentication. Event mutation by consumer is not evidence of backend activity.

progress.all_totals: None; no derived percentage or inferred work total. 100% never establishes completion.
progress.gzip: GzipCumulativeProcessedBytes from native checkpoint.usage.processed; includes prior calls on same Budget, input supply/read-ahead and actual output, including failures. Native usage snapshot also retained.
progress.ustar: UstarInputOffset { pass } and UstarEntryIndex { pass } are cursor/index observations with original checkpoint timing, not cross-pass cumulative bytes or completed item counts. Native Completed.usage remains authoritative.
progress.zip: ZipInputOffset { entry } is the original before-input checkpoint offset; ZipOutputExtent is the existing buffer extent before the pending write, not successful pending bytes. Seek/rewrite are not added as new output. No native final Usage exists; do not fabricate one.
progress.comparison: Metrics and phases are distinct; never compare them as one shared processed counter.

control.request: Cancellation::request() is monotonic/idempotent and reports whether it set the flag first. It is a request, not an actual cancellation result.
control.poll_order: At an existing native checkpoint, allocate event stamp and invoke the native-typed observer first. Observer Err is returned unchanged. Only observer Ok is followed by polling the request flag and returning native Stop::Cancelled. No extra checks before entering or after returning from the native module.
control.priority: Preserve native request validation, pre/post callback deadline checks, GZip failed-output charging/backend precedence, USTAR selection-error immediate return and ZIP sticky first Failure. Budget stays Budget; do not infer Deadline.
control.snapshot: Terminal cancellation_requested is a snapshot at return construction; cancellation_forwarded means this handle was observed and converted to Stop::Cancelled at a checkpoint. Neither overrides actual native result. Explicit observer cancellation may yield Cancelled with forwarded=false.
control.late_request: A request after the final checkpoint can coexist with success. A request after terminal creation does not mutate that terminal. Native errors before a checkpoint may coexist with requested=true and forwarded=false.
control.limits: Cooperative only. No preemption or all-panic/OOM recovery. Callback time remains included in native timing. A panic may produce no Terminal.

result.only_success: MemoryValidated means native operation returned successfully under the identified frozen policy; no additional round-trip validation is claimed for ZIP creation. Only private adapter code constructs this wrapper.
result.failure: No Completed payload. Failure.native owns the exact returned typed error; Failure.adapter independently preserves sequence faults, never overwriting native cause.
result.origin: Terminal policy identifies the frozen implementation mapping in sources.json: GzipSingleMemberV1, UstarLinuxV1, ZipAsciiCreateV1.
limits_preserved: GZip exact single member/EOF, unselected full decode, caller-shared Budget retained across retries
USTAR Linux raw UTF-8 policy, Windows Unsupported, exact string IDs and ContentVerification::Unavailable retained in Completed
ZIP existing ASCII name policy and already-coarsened Failure::Engine retained; underlying backend details cannot be recovered by the adapter
result.callback_types: GZip original Stop::Callback(E) -> Error::Callback(E); USTAR select E -> Error::Selection(E). ZIP/USTAR checkpoint APIs only support Cancelled/Deadline, not arbitrary E; observer signature reflects that limitation.
result.no_promotion: No ProtocolObserved, Published, mock PR39 type, OS receipt or external cleanup evidence. ProcessCleanup::NotApplicable means no process resource was created by this adapter; it does not claim every upstream allocation/Drop/panic is recovered.

dependency_policy.direct: Three existing path libraries only. All 42 registry package records match the union of original locks. Linux selected 29 package feature sets equal original selected union.
dependency_policy.licenses: Own code MIT; raw cache-matched third-party license bytes and hashes listed in dependencies.json/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt. Scope is Linux selected packages, not final all-platform distribution.
dependency_policy.unchanged: Original source/test/lock/manifest bytes preserved. No source include or production copy into adapter, no new codec/crypto or external package.

validation.build: locked/offline --lib, exit 0, final build without warnings
validation.format: rustfmt check required on adapter only
validation.originals: 60 imported source/test blobs compared to fixed GitHub trees before and after build
validation.runtime: No adapter regression or original regression rerun. Existing module results belong to their original heads only.
not_claimed: Dynamic overflow coverage; ID/sequence exhaustion branches have no public injection API

Pre-requested cancellation, callback error precedence, cancel from callback, late cancellation retaining success/error
Event exact sequence, no-checkpoint native error terminal zero, new operation stale progress/terminal ignored
Receiver duplicates/gaps/reversal/post-terminal rejection without payload application
Native policy/Usage/ContentVerification preservation, no protocol/publishing promotion
